subject: Re: Liability cap structure — pro rata vs aggregate
messages:

Subject: MSA redlines: Limitation of liability

Attached are Acme's redlines to the MSA and Order Form — key points below so you can circle back quickly with legal:

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Laura / Marissa — forwarding Acme's redlines (attached). Highlights from their asks: aggregate 3x fees or $5M floor; want consequential damages removed for data loss. They have procurement timelines and want this wrapped this week.

My thinking (high level): unacceptable to remove consequential damages exclusion outright — that exposes us to open-ended exposure. We can be flexible on how cap is calculated, but prefer a per-contract-year (resetting) cap tied to billed fees for that year with an annual multiplier rather than a single life-of-contract aggregate. Practical options to propose: 

- Option A (vendor-friendly): Per contract year cap = greater of $1,000,000 or 1x fees billed in that year (resets each year).
- Option B (compromise): Per contract year cap = greater of $1,500,000 or 1.5x fees billed in that year (resets each year) + explicit carveouts for IP infringement / willful misconduct (still excluded from cap).
- Option C (their ask but scaled): Aggregate cap = greater of $2,000,000 or 2x total fees paid in the prior 12 months (one-time cumulative).

Please advise which approach we can defend operationally and legally. If we commit to a reset-each-year approach, explain the billing/metrics we should reference (invoice window vs calendar year). Also flag whether we should allow a narrowly-tailored consequential damages exposure for data loss tied to confirmed production incidents (e.g., direct remediation costs capped).

I attached a quick counter proposal template: Redwood_counter_cap_options.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20m call with Acme legal if that speeds resolution.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-15T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines: Limitation of liability

Karthik / Marissa — reviewed Acme's redlines and your proposed options. High-level legal posture below; happy to join the call.

1) Consequential damages: We should maintain the exclusion for consequential, incidental, and special damages as a baseline. Removing it entirely creates an unbounded exposure (claims for lost business, lost profits, etc.). If the counterparty insists on a carve for "data loss," negotiate a narrowly tailored remedy: direct remediation costs or reasonable cost to restore data, capped and evidenced (e.g., third-party recovery invoices). Do not accept an open-ended consequential damages carveout.

2) Cap structure — pros/cons: 
- Aggregate (life-of-contract) cap: simpler but risks large one-off exposure; difficult to forecast for high-growth customers.
- Per-contract-year (resetting) cap: aligns with billing and is easier to budget; preferred for SaaS-like recurring vendors. We can justify a per-year cap tied to fees for that year.

3) Multipliers & floors: Market practice varies. For enterprise SaaS in regulated customers, a 1x to 2x annual multiplier is defensible. Floors ($1M+ depending on revenue/usage) are common. Given Acme's ask (3x / $5M), recommend starting with a firm position: per-year cap = greater of $1,000,000 or 1x fees for that year, with the ability to escalate to 1.5x for strategic deals (requires legal approval). If they push aggregate, offer a scaled aggregate as a concession: greater of $2,000,000 or 2x prior 12 months fees.

4) Carveouts: Maintain carveouts for IP infringement and willful misconduct. For injunctive relief or equitable remedies, note that injunctive relief is typically uncapped (we should acknowledge that in language).

5) Draft language suggestions: I will prepare redline language that: (a) defines "fees for the applicable Contract Year" and references the invoice window; (b) preserves consequential damage exclusion but adds a narrowly drawn exception for documented data restoration costs (subject to receipts); (c) specifies that injunctive relief and IP indemnity remain outside the cap.

Next step: I can redline the MSA with Option B (1.5x annual / $1.5M floor) and a narrowly defined data-restoration carve if you want to present a compromise. If you prefer to be more conservative, present Option A.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-16T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: Limitation of liability — Redwood counterproposal

Jordan — thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround. We reviewed with legal and prepared a counter that tries to bridge both sides and keeps procurement timelines in mind. High-level proposal below; redline attached for your review.

Proposal (compromise):
- Liability cap: Per Contract Year (resets each year). Cap = greater of (i) $1,500,000 OR (ii) 1.5x Fees billed for that Contract Year.
- Carveouts: IP infringement, willful misconduct, and injunctive relief are excluded from the cap (i.e., remain uncapped where applicable).
- Consequential damages: exclusion remains in place for consequential, incidental, special, and punitive damages. Narrow data-restoration carve: Redwood will be liable for reasonable documented costs to restore or recover customer data resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or a confirmed production incident, subject to receipts and a sub-cap of $250,000 per incident.

We believe this is a fair middle ground: it gives Acme a meaningful remedy bucket tied to spend while limiting open-ended exposure for Redwood. If you prefer an aggregate (life-of-contract) formulation, we can offer aggregate = greater of $2,000,000 OR 2x fees paid in prior 12 months as a fall-back, but we would prefer the annual reset.

Next steps: please review the attached redline (OrderForm-Redline-20270616.docx) and let us know if Acme legal wants to accept Option B or discuss on a short call. We can also push this through DocuSign once redlines are agreed.
